silhouette.reason: Torpedo body, tall first dorsal, crescent caudal, pectorals and five gill slits read as a great white from every view.
fixes: a more lunate caudal with the lower lobe nearly as long as the upper

proportions.reason: 4.5 m TL with the sourced girth and dorsal position; the pectoral fins are paper-thin plates (a line in FRONT) and the snout is slightly pointed for a white shark.
fixes: give the pectorals a root thickness (~6 % of chord) tapering to the edge

materials.reason: Countershading grey over white with a ragged boundary reads; skin is one uniform satin with fine speckle; the eye is a glossy black ball with no rim.
fixes: denticle micro-normal and slight sheen variation over the flank
an eyelid rim and darker pupil ring around the eye

detail.reason: Gill slits, teeth row, pores on the snout, pelvic and second dorsal fins; no lateral line, claspers or fin-edge darkening.
fixes: dark pectoral tips and trailing edges
the lateral line and caudal keels

wear.reason: Pink scratch scars on the back tell a fighting history.
fixes: a torn notch in the first dorsal

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 keeps outline and countershading; the white boundary straightens to a hard edge.
fixes: keep the boundary wave at LOD2 by colouring along a jagged vertex row

technical.reason: QA clean; 61k / 7k / 680 tris across 7 parts; the LOD1 step is steep (8.7×).
fixes: raise LOD1 to ~15k so the fins and gills survive the first switch
